questions.stem: Which proper nouns must be capitalized according to the lecture?
options: Days and months (Monday, September)
Names of hospitals (St Mary's Hospital)
Holidays
Common nouns such as "hospital" in "admitted to the hospital"
questions.explanation: Names of people, places, days, months, holidays and institutions are capitalized. "the hospital" used as a common noun is not.

questions.stem: Which drug names are correctly written?
options: metformin
Prozac
Aspirin (used as a generic name mid-sentence)
diazepam
questions.explanation: Generic names are lowercase (aspirin, diazepam, metformin); brand names are capitalized (Prozac, Lipitor).

questions.stem: About generic and brand drug names:
options: Generic names are nonproprietary and lowercase
Brand names are proprietary and capitalized
The brand name should be preferred in formal medical writing
Disulfiram is generic; Antabuse is its brand name
questions.explanation: Use the generic name unless there is a specific clinical reason to use the brand name; generic names are preferred in most formal writing.

questions.stem: Which eponymous diseases are written correctly?
options: Alzheimer's disease
Down syndrome
Parkinson's Disease
tourette syndrome
questions.explanation: The person's name is capitalized; "disease" or "syndrome" is not.

options: Some style guides, including SNOMED CT, recommend omitting it
"Down syndrome" is preferred to "Down's syndrome" by those guides
You should check your institution's preferred style
The apostrophe is compulsory in every style guide
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that SNOMED CT and others omit the apostrophe and advises following the institution's style.

questions.stem: Which disease names are correctly capitalized?
options: Lyme disease
West Nile virus
Pneumonia (mid-sentence)
leukemia
questions.explanation: Diseases named after places are usually capitalized; common diseases (pneumonia, leukemia, cancer) are not.

options: The patient was diagnosed with cancer of the colon.
The patient was diagnosed with Cancer of the Colon.
The patient was diagnosed with Hypertension.
The patient has Type 2 Diabetes and Migraine.
questions.explanation: Most diseases are not capitalized unless they include a proper name.

options: Their letters are almost always capitalized (MRI, ECG, GP)
"The mri scan showed no abnormalities" is correct
ENT stands for Ear, Nose, and Throat
NHS and CDC are written in capitals
questions.explanation: Acronyms are capitalized: MRI, CT, ECG, ENT, ICU, ER, GP, WHO, CDC, NHS.

options: "She was referred to the cardiology department" is correct
"He specializes in Neurology" is correct
"She works in the Department of Cardiology at St Mary's Hospital" is correct
Specialties are always capitalized
questions.explanation: Specialties are lowercase as common nouns and capitalized only as part of a proper name or department title.

questions.stem: Which uses of professional titles are correct?
options: Dr Smith examined the patient.
Professor Jones presented the case.
The Nurse administered the medication.
The doctor examined the patient.
questions.explanation: Titles are capitalized before a name, as part of it; used as common nouns (the doctor, the nurse) they are lowercase.

options: The genus is capitalized and the species is lowercase
Both parts are italicized in print
After the first full use the genus may be abbreviated: S. aureus
The convention follows ordinary English capitalization rules
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature follows an international convention independent of ordinary English rules.

options: Blood cultures were positive for Escherichia coli.
The wound swab grew staphylococcus Aureus.
She had a streptococcal throat infection.
The patient's infection was Staphylococcal.
questions.explanation: Genus capital + species lowercase. Adjectival forms (staphylococcal, streptococcal) are lowercase and not italic.

options: Title case capitalizes all major words but not articles or short prepositions (unless first)
Sentence case capitalizes only the first word and proper nouns
Most hospital templates use sentence case for section headings
Mixing both conventions within one document is recommended
questions.explanation: Title case for the document title, sentence case for section headings ("Reason for admission"); consistency within a document is essential.

questions.stem: "Discharge summary for Mrs Alia Thompson" is written in:
options: Sentence case
Title case
All capitals
Lowercase
questions.explanation: Only the first word and proper nouns are capitalized. In title case it would be "Discharge Summary for Mrs Alia Thompson".

questions.stem: Which corrections of "he was admitted to st mary's hospital on friday. The mri was normal." are right?
options: St Mary's Hospital
Friday
MRI
Hospital should stay lowercase because it is a common noun
questions.explanation: Hospital is part of the institution's proper name here; days and acronyms are capitalized; the sentence also starts with a capital (He).

questions.stem: Why does capitalization matter in medical writing, according to the lecture?
options: It distinguishes a specific product (brand) from a general medication (generic)
It distinguishes a disease from a person's name (Parkinson's)
It serves clarity and safety
The rules are arbitrary conventions with no clinical function
questions.explanation: The conclusion stresses that the rules are not arbitrary but serve clarity and safety.
